text: An incident of rwb-access is a record and not a table: one entry of the local decision-record chain of DP-03 for the open, carrying the steps DETECTED and HELD, and one entry for the closure, carrying the steps FIXED, RECORDED and REPORTED, each written in the same transaction as its idempotency row. The state is derived from the entries - OPEN after the first and CLOSED after the second - and is never stored. The incident id is minted by this service and is opaque to every consumer. The three operations are POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/incidents, POST /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/incidents/{incidentId}/closure and GET /api/recovery/access/v1/admin/incidents/{incidentId}, and the incident surface is composed at the edge by the gateway-bff route because no source names an incident screen. The detection signal stays with RWB-PLT-OBS: the reference and the detection time are entered on the surface, because TSD P4 v3 T5.1 declares no interface from the observability platform to P4.
why: No source contains an incident entity, an incident operation or an incident screen, and the monolith kept the path inside one administration process, so the record, the paths, the state model and the composition of the surface have to be fixed before the story can be built; leaving them open would stop the wave and inviting the record into a new table of this service would add a table the ownership map does not have.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-017 (story statement, AC1 detect hold fix record report, screens SCR-39 and SCR-41); FSD P4 v3 A2.28.1 to A2.28.3 and A2.28.4; TSD P4 v3 T3.1 (five P4 tables), T5.1 (INT-21 and INT-22 only), T6.1 and appendix T-A.1; the context pack rows for P4 (four REST operations, no event, JOB-18); DP-03 and DP-19; Template and Rules R5.7 Day-1 rule.
confirm: Solution architect, the tech lead of rwb-access and the owner of the decision-record library at the contract review of RWB-P4-E8017-CON
impact: If the edition of an incident must be a table of its own, the ownership map gains a table, the Flyway story of this service changes and the read becomes a query rather than a chain read; the step set, the states and the three paths do not change.

text: The incident path is authorised by the Platform administration letters of TSD P4 v3 T6.1: C on the open, U on the closure and R on the read, held by RW-PLATADM as CRUD, RW-SECADM as CRUDA, RW-AUDIT and RW-COE as R and by the case roles as a dash. The legacy permission table of RWB-E8-017, which gives Rules and parameters C to RW-COE and A to RW-RISK, is the rule-change right set of the same chapter and not this feature's; R-PREC puts the Technical Specifications above the story master. A caller without the letter is refused 403 with MSG-P4-002, and a caller holding a dash in every held area is answered 404 with MSG-P4-003 on the read. The tribe lead, named as a secondary role by FSD P4 v3 A2.28.3.3, reads only where its R is in force in the area and writes nothing.
why: Three sources disagree on who may open an incident: the legacy table names Rules and parameters letters that belong to the rule-change journey, the FSD makes the platform administrator primary, and the technical specification, which outranks the story master, gives that role CRUD in Platform administration and R only in Rules and parameters; a story that silently kept the legacy letters would contradict the matrix, and one that dropped the platform administrator would contradict the FSD.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-017 permission checks; FSD P4 v3 A2.28.3.3 roles and permissions; TSD P4 v3 T6.1 RBAC matrix and T6.2; Template and Rules R3 R-PREC and R5.5 DP-08 (the matrix is data); MSG-P4-002 and MSG-P4-003 in the legacy message table.
confirm: Solution architect with the owner of the permission matrix and the security administrator at the P4 design review
impact: If the matrix is later changed, only the permission rows and the SIT users of the tests change and no code does; if the legacy letters were kept instead, the platform administrator would be refused the path it owns and the story would not meet FEAT-ADM-12.

text: A step of an incident is written under the administrative-change record code of the local decision-record library of DP-03, with the incident id in the reference field of the entry, the steps of the entry in its actions, the incident reference, the detection or resolution time, the held areas with their rights and scopes, the reason, the fix reference, the report reference and the parameters version in its inputs reference, and with no case id. The field-level shape of a step inside the entry and the format of the incident id are fixed with the ledger owner before the baseline of RWB-P4-E8017-CON is tagged, and the incident id remains opaque to every consumer.
why: The sources fix the decision codes of a case decision and of an access event and give no code for an administrative step, and the entry must be findable by the identifier the surface and audit quote; the legacy criterion nevertheless requires the result to be written to the decision log with the rule version, so a code and a field placement have to be fixed to test it.
read: Legacy RWB-E8-017 AC1 and AC2; TSD P4 v3 T6.3 (a change log entry is append only, with the version label, the status change, the author or approver and the time); Logical Data Model and Data Dictionary v8 DF-DEC-003 for the decision code and DF-DEC-008 for the reference field; DP-03 and the access-event codes AC-READ, AC-DENY and AC-EXPT already in use.
confirm: Tech lead of rwb-access with the owner of the decision-record library and the Internal audit representative
impact: A different code or a different field placement changes the value written on every step entry and the filter audit uses; the entry would still be found by its incident id, and the steps, the states and the answers do not change.
